dedupe_keys.name: hurricane irene 2011 north shore long island jewish health system evacuation of three hospitals

description: This case describes how the North Shore-Long Island Jewish Health System, a large integrated network in New York, evacuated three of its hospitals at high risk of flooding before Hurricane Irene in August 2011. The published case study reports that 947 patients were evacuated, transported and placed in other facilities without any deaths or serious injuries. The producer is the author, C. Verni, writing in Health Affairs (2012). Coverage is the health system's hospitals in the New York region during one storm. The system's success rested on an evacuation plan refined through full-scale exercises held after Hurricane Katrina, in which it learned to abandon one-to-one matching of patients to regional beds in favour of moving groups of patients with similar needs to facilities able to take them. Lessons included the need for automated patient tracking with bar-coded wristbands and for more trained backup staff in the emergency operations centre, and the author recommends that state and federal policy makers mandate full-scale interfacility evacuation drills. The abstract is available free on Europe PMC; the full article is behind the Health Affairs paywall. Caveats: this is a single-system account written from the system's perspective, and it gives no timeline data or transport counts by mode. Simulation uses: validating hospital evacuation and patient allocation models, and comparing matching rules for transfers. Related records: the Hurricane Sandy case (case_study-hurricane-sandy-nyc-hospital-evacuations) shows the same region a year later.
